I generally enjoyed playing this game, its strongest points being storyline and characters (both PC and NPC).

Pros: 1. There is a coherent storyline, with outcomes strongly contingent on in-game decisions. 2. Basic combat is fairly easy to master. 3. The characters are distinctive in temperament and ability, frequently amusing, and their reactions and behaviour are relevant to outcomes. 4. The game is fairly easy to mod, mostly through the DAO Modmanager, available on Nexus. 5. Commitment to one path of character specialization or another gives higher returns than attempting a generalist playstyle. 6. Replayability is pretty good, though ultimately you are still stuck with the linear narrative.

Cons: 1. Even by the standards of its release date the sets and artistry are nothing spectacular. 2. If you have my lazy playstyle, navigating the tactics menu (which is a powerful game tool and make battles flow smoothly) is difficult, tedious, and irritating. Failure to do so makes combat a process of pause, issue orders, unpause, assess, pause, issue new orders, repeat. 3. By the late game, the quests have become repetitious, and yet must be completed to advance the narrative. 4. As a linear (as opposed to open world) game, you must go to all lengths to acquire every scrap of loot and experience in order to acquire the best equipment and defeat the top adversaries.

It is physically painful for me to give this masterpiece a thumbs-down, but the state of it is un-purchasable. Nonstop game-breaking crashes. If Bioware doesn't care to this degree, it should release it to the community to preserve.

Before playing this game, I'd been a longtime fan of similar media set in high fantasy worlds, and had been debating getting the game. I read a little about the characters, and fell in love with a handful, then decided to buy it. And, honestly? I would've spent $60 on this game. The plot rarely feels stale, although I will admit, some portions are better than others- the Alienage backstory is a thousand times better than the human noble, fight me. The game can be extremely challenging or a quick breeze, thanks to adjustable difficulty. The characters, especially the main party (Alastair, Morrigan, Leliana, Sten, Zevran, Wynne, and Oghren) are rounded out and all feel real, and even those not in the spotlight (Loghain, Duncan, Flemeth, most of the Dalish, etc) are all very well done as well. It's rare for video games to have good voice acting, I've found, but this game excells with it. The graphics can occasionally cause a problem, but it's nothing mods can't fix.

Overall? 10/10. Get it. Right now. What are you waiting for.

DA:O is one of the most unique experiences I have ever played. I have always liked RPG games, but very few times have I gotten engaged with the story, world or characters around me. They were simply a way to advance with the gameplay. When I played DA:O for the first time, my perspective changed drastically.

From the start of the character creation, until the end of the story, It feels we are playing a genuine and unique experience to every player. Our class, race and origin story change how we interact with multiple npc's and how certain story events are played.

This type of decision-making directly changes how the game evolves. To the point of not having a complete party in the endgame. Death, betrayal, romances and entire quest lines are different in each run.

The gameplay may feel a bit clunky by today's standards, but the tactic approach to combat gets more satisfying with time. Skill trees uniqueness makes builds feel diverse (at least for the mage) and the spell combination system is much better than the sequels.

I will not speak about the lore, in-game story/lore. DA:O is a journey that deserves to be played and is better if you know nothing about the franchise, something that I wish I could do again.

It's a classic CRPG, and I highly recommend it if you're interested in complex, medieval, grimdark stories and settings.

I finished this game last night live on stream. It took me about 3 weeks of playing for about 3/4 hours per night. It is a fantastic game with an incredibly amazing storyline and well thought out characters. The game is left open for replayability because of the way you can a) pick different characters/background b) the way you can delivery yourself to the AI in the game and c) the difficulties. I played the game on Normal throughout, however I could easily go back and play it on Easy for a more RPG style type of game or on a higher difficulty for a more stategic style type of game, which I will most likely do.
The music as well in the game is fantastic.

I would highly recommend this game for anyone who enjoys diving into a vast world with lots of story and characters where you can pick how you play! 10/10 from me!

Still one of the greatest RPGs of all time. Masterful worldbuilding, complex morality and pretty meaningful choices make DA:O an instant favorite. Doesn't hurt that the strategy/RTS combat is well done too (except mana clash, nerf that shit).

Though it's an older game and the graphics are outdated it's still a fun game to play around with. There are plenty of quests to do and and lots of lore and challenges to uncover. I tend to use a controller but this game has pushed me in the direction of keyboard and mouse, which is fine with me. I think anyone with a bit of nostalgia will enjoy diving into this classic game.

This is the game you should buy, if you're looking for fantasy RPG in an immersive and entertaining world. It might not have aged brilliatnly in so far as graphics and AI stand, but that dosen't detract from the game's overall feel, atmospher and sheer enjoyability.

I absolutely love this game. The characters are all interesting (Shale is my favorite companion, even though he is extremely cynical) and will occasionally banter with each other. Gameplay is standard for a good D&D style RPG (though I feel the hotbar is too short). The classes are all unique, with four specializations that each have their own benefits, a few of which blur the boundaries between classes (examples being Templar and the mage knight one). The game does have an issue with not guiding you towards the best location for your level, but it does mean you can tackle challenges in any order you want. The game does have a detail that has me terrified to continue a few saves simply because of the black pulsating stain on my map slowly growing out to areas I have to go to or I have not fully completed due to quest requirements. There are some issues with certain quests being unable to complete due to requiring certain talents among your party that you may miss due to xp scaling or poor planning. Due to various issues with the game, I do recommend using mods to improve upon bugs and glitches as well as add anything you personally feel is missing (I recommend the lock bash mod).

Dragon Age: Origins - Ultimate Edition is an exceptional and epic fantasy role playing game. It is a perfect combination of old school (Baldur's Gate, Icewind Dale, etc...) and modern western rpgs. It has a rich universe that tries to differentiates itself from the usual Tolkien bases (though I believe it is still very close to the classics... Replace Darkspawns with evil Orcs, and Archdemon with Sauron... But that is not a turn off at all...)

The tactical gameplay is very fun, the player is at the center of the story line and the many dialogues make you actually care about the other characters and NPCs. There are several important choices that significantly change the story line. I am curious to know what's Bioware's canon for this game. Last but not least, this Ultimate Edition has all the DLCs and I really enjoyed most of them (Awakening is a respectable +20 hours campaign).

I will definitely miss the epic tale of my Grey Warden but I am also looking forward to discover the story of Hawke and the Inquisitor (DA2 & 3)! I wish they were available on Steam, but hey, you can't have everything, haha!

Verdict: 9.5/10
